item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 40 - Shandon Anderson (1999-2000)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the seventh of eight who wore the No. 40, Shandon Anderson. After ending his college career at Georgia, Anderson was picked up with the 54th overall selection of the 1996 NBA Draft by the Utah Jazz. The Atlanta, Georgia native played the first 3 seasons of his pro career with Utah, coming to an end when he signed with the Houston Rockets in 1999. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to the New York Knicks in 2001. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Anderson wore only jersey No. 40 and put up 10.5 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.6 assists, and 1.1 steals per game, All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - James Ennis III
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is James Ennis III. An alum of Cal State Long Beach, he was picked up with the 50th overall selection of the 2013 NBA Draft by the Atlanta Hawks. The Ventura, California native played the first season of his NBA career with the Miami Heat instead. He also played for the Memphis Grizzlies , New Orleans Pelicans , Griz again, Detroit Pistons , Houston Rockets , Philadelphia 76ers , and Orlando Magic before he signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2021. His stay with the team lasted until he signed with the Los Angeles Clippers a few weeks later. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Ennis put up 2.5 points and as many rebounds per game. item.title: Former Rice football coach and player Ray Alborn dies at age 87
item.description: Rice coach Ray Alborn is carried off the field after the Owls beat UH in 1980. (Sam C. Pierson Jr./Houston Chronicle) Former Rice football coach Ray Alborn, who also played for the Owls, died on Thursday, the school announced. He was 87. Alborn coached the Owls from 1978-83. His best season was in 1980 when Rice went 5-6 with wins over LSU, TCU, Texas A&M, Arkansas and Houston. Overall, he was 13-53 on South Main. Alborn, who played in high school at Houston Lamar, signed to play with Rice in 1957. His junior season, Alborn was a starter at defensive tackle and helped the Owls to the Sugar Bowl. He was a team captain as a senior. Alborn started his coaching career at junior highs in the Houston area before becoming head coach at Sharpstown in 1969. He returned to Rice in 1972 as a defensive line coach on Al Conover's staff. He was defensive coordinator for Homer Rice. After Rice, Alborn coached the defensive tackles for Jack Pardee with the Houston Gamblers of the USFL. He coached Lamar University from 1986-89 and was 13-30 overall, including 5-5 in 1989 before the school opted to drop football. Alborn returned to coaching in 1998 at Lamar Consolidated. He led the Mustangs to their first winning season in 18 years in 1999 and a spot in the playoffs. A visitation will be held from 6-8 p.m. on Wednesday in Sugar Land at Settegast-Kopf Co. at 15015 Southwest Freeway. A memorial service will be at 11 a.m. on Thursday at Sugar Land Methodist Church at 431 Eldridge Road. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Sewickley Academy captures fifth WPIAL girls soccer title in program history
item.description: PITTSBURGH — When top-seeded Sewickley Academy hit the pitch for the WPIAL Class 1A girls high school soccer championship match against No. 2 Winchester, it lost just one match since its defeat in last year’s finals, falling in the quarterfinals of the PIAA playoffs. That impressive streak continued Friday, November 6 at F.N.B. Stadium as Sewickley Academy knocked off Winchester Thurston 2-0 to claim its fifth WPIAL championship in program history and its first title since 2004. “When I was a freshman, winning a playoff game, let alone playing and winning a WPIAL championship, was something that I did not think was possible,” senior forward Emma Eannarino said. “To be here and put together the year that we’ve had, it has shown how much we have grown as a group and how hard we work for everything.” Last season in the title game, Sewickley Academy (19-0-0) was shut out by Bentworth and fell in heartbreaking fashion, after surrendering a late goal. But in this year’s match, Sewickley Academy was the aggressor from the jump and was backed by a stellar back line. The Panthers wasted little time to get on the board, with Sewickley Academy taking the early lead after midfielder Claire Karsman crossed a ball inside the box and was finished off by fellow sophomore striker Sarah Merryman. “We talked heading into this about getting that first goal on the board,” Sewickley Academy head coach Gary Weber said. “Our back line has been solid all year and the backs have been spectacular.” Required Reading: WPIAL high school football playoffs Beaver Valley live score updates Required Reading: Beaver Valley teams gear up for WPIAL high school soccer championships Required Reading: OLSH girls high school volleyball eyeing first WPIAL championship After recording an assist in the match’s first goal, Karsman put up a crucial insurance tally in the 59th minute, manoeuvring her way inside the box and putting it past the Winchester Thurston (18-3-0) goalkeeper into the top left corner of the net. “I was getting pushed around down in the box but saved the ball from going out,” Karsman said. “Once I turned, I saw the goal and just shot it. Freshman goalkeeper Courtney Weinreich recorded a clean sheet, making a multitude of saves from long and close range. “It was a tough night to play in goal,” Weber said. “Balls were skipping and flying from all different directions. The girl in front of her, Lila Peluso, is also a freshman and has stepped up well after our starting defender went out with a concussion earlier.” With the win, Sewickley Academy will now set its sights on the PIAA playoffs, as it will take on the runner-up of District V at a site and time to be determined on Tuesday, November 10. item.title: Could Sunday Be Jonathan Taylor’s Final Game? Colts $44 Million Star Addresses Trade Noise
item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor may be playing his final game with the team this Sunday. Ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, the 2–6 Colts have already started changing their roster by trading away veteran stars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Those moves have put Taylor at the center of intense trade speculation. The Colts host the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. While rumors suggest this could be Taylor’s last appearance for Indianapolis, he told reporters on Thursday that he has not requested a trade. Jonathan Taylor addresses Colts’ fire sale and trade deadline speculation Addressing the heavy internet speculation on Thursday, Taylor got brutally honest about the psychological toll of the unresolved rumors. Nov 9, 2025; Berlin, Germany; Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) is interviewed on the field after defeating the Atlanta Falcons in the NFL Berlin Game at Olympic Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images “Everybody wants clarity,” Taylor admitted during a locker room interview . “No one wants uncertainty. The past couple weeks, it’s kind of been the same thing, but it won’t be until Tuesday at that time where then you’ll know exactly what’s going on, exactly what the verdict is. You just have to continue to go to work… and then let the chips fall where they may.” The massive shift inside the locker room started when the front office fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard. Under interim leadership, the Colts lost to the Minnesota Vikings, dropping their record to 2–5. Shortly after, the team made the rebuild by trading away star guard Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. The pressure surrounding Taylor intensified after a blowout 42–7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, where he had just eight carries for 23 yards. While head coach Shane Steichen stated that Taylor’s role will not change this Sunday against Dallas, the light workload led to speculation that the team was protecting its star asset for a trade. However, his big contract makes a trade complicated for the front office. He is currently playing on a two-year, $44 million extension that carries $39 million in guarantees. According to league insiders, the Colts are demanding a premium, “Christian McCaffrey-style” package of multiple premium draft picks to let their top offensive star go. On Wednesday, the 28-year-old wideout filed paperwork to return from the reserve/left squad list, having sat out since his Oct. 20, 2024 ACL tear. Amid this, GM John Lynch refuses to fully close the door on a reunion. John Lynch says Brandon Aiyuk reunion possible amid $13M bonus hurdle This sudden influx of options is a massive shift from the team’s initial stance. item.title: Shenendehowa girls' volleyball continues Section 2 title streak
item.description: Shenendehowa celebrates after beating Saratoga in the Section 2, Class AAA finals on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - The Shenendehowa girls' volleyball team boasts a powerhouse up front, with several weapons the Mustangs can call on to make an impact. In Friday's Section 2 Class AAA championship, Shenendehowa's potent offense was the focus once again as the top-seeded Mustangs swept past No. 2 Saratoga Springs in straight sets 25-13, 25-14, 25-16, at Saratoga Springs High School. "It makes it so fun because the defense doesn't really have one person to focus on," Shenendehowa coach Lori Kessler said. "They have to focus on three hitting options at all times, and running a 6-2 with two great setters, they're spreading it out. It's such a great part of our offense." Shenendehowa sophomores Melanie Tubbs and Claire Siska combined for 18 kills, junior Hadley Ennist added 10 kills and 11 assists, and senior Ava Los chipped in five kills. Shenendehowa, the top-ranked team in the state Class AAA poll, pushed its sectional title win streak to six with. The four most recent championships have come in Class AAA since the state expanded to a six-classification system. "It's a completely new team than what we've had in the past," Ennist said. "It's a ton of younger girls and some seniors. It's just such a big mix and honestly, we're doing a great job together. It's so fun to be able to play with such a variety of ages and abilities out there." Key moment Shenendehowa trailed 6-5 in the second set, but used a pair of runs to gain control. The Mustangs used a 7-0 spurt to grab a 12-6 lead, and Ennist set up sophomore Leah Alfandre for a kill to cap a 5-1 run which provided Shenendehowa its first double-digit lead of the set, 17-7. "Those were really big for us, especially in a game this competitive," Ennist said. "If you do get into a little bit of a rut, you still have so much time to come out of it, and I think we did a really great job of getting that lead." Star of the game Shenendehowa freshman setter Kyli Kessler, the coach's daughter, turned in a stellar all-around performance. Kessler finished with 19 assists, 12 service points, including a pair of aces, and nine digs. "She works hard year-round on her game," Lori Kessler said of her daughter. "I think that she really wanted to prove herself this season, and I think that her being surrounded by the girls, by the great passing and the great hitters, makes her job a little bit easier for her. But regardless, she's still an everyday hard worker that if something feels off, she's the first one out there that wants to fix it and make it better for everybody." item.title: ‘That’s what they wanted’: Ryan Clark claims ESPN used Sophie Cunningham interview to impress conservatives
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Clark has had plenty to say about how his time at ESPN came to an end. The former NFL analyst was laid off in July, and he found out while he was still on the air. Now, Clark is suggesting that the way it all played out was planned. Clark has previously made it clear that he believes ESPN wanted his firing to become a story. Now, he’s arguing that it used an interview with Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham to show it was changing direction. Clark’s ESPN exit Clark was pulled off the set of NFL Live in the middle of the show on July 20. ESPN had planned to tell him the next day as part of a wider round of layoffs, but word of his departure got out first. OutKick, the conservative-leaning outlet owned by Fox that had long been critical of Clark, had the story before it was published elsewhere. OutKick’s Bobby Burack said that the outlet gave ESPN an hour’s notice so the network could tell Clark itself, according to Awful Announcing . ESPN then moved to tell Clark before he could find out on social media. A day later, ESPN published a profile of Cunningham , in which the Indiana Fever guard said she supports keeping transgender athletes out of girls’ and women’s sports. “I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men,” Cunningham told ESPN. Cunningham also said she had received “a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans,” adding, “I never once said that.” The comments made her one of the biggest stories in the WNBA, and she has since insisted her political views are “right in the middle.” Clark has already called his firing “purposeful,” saying on The Breakfast Club earlier this fall that ESPN handled it in a way that was meant to humiliate him. ‘That’s what they wanted’ On Thursday, Clark took things a step further during an appearance on All The Smoke . He argued that ESPN wanted conservative outlets like OutKick to see his firing and the Cunningham interview as a sign that the network was changing its brand. “Sophie Cunningham says something and they say, ‘A great brand switch for ESPN,'” Clark said. He added that the message was, “Ryan Clark was fired this week and now Sophie Cunningham leads the news.” “That’s what they wanted. That’s why you leaked it to them,” Clark said. Clark admitted that he should have seen it coming, saying that his “antenna should have been up more.” But he also said that “there was nothing I could change.” He pointed to signs that he was being phased out, including ESPN’s promotional rollout for its Super Bowl coverage. “There was a commercial first and when they did the commercial Marcus [Spears] and Laura [Rutledge] were in it,” Clark said. “I’m not involved.” “So I say all that to say, that this was the plan,” he added. item.title: Broncos Legend Blasts ‘Delusional’ Chiefs Fans After Patrick Mahomes TD Wiped Out
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs appeared to secure a dramatic, last-second victory over the Denver Broncos on Sunday when Patrick Mahomes connected with Emmett Johnson for a game-winning touchdown. Instead, a false start penalty on right tackle Jaylon Moore wiped out the score. On the next play, Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes to seal a 28-24 win for Denver, giving the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. Afterward, furious Chiefs fans blamed the referees on social media. But former Broncos safety Justin Simmons fired back with a harsh response. Justin Simmons blasts Chiefs fans defending Patrick Mahomes Simmons, who played eight years in Denver, dismissed fans’ complaints regarding the late-game penalty, stating that Kansas City fans had no grounds to be upset and accusing them of benefiting from officiating. Oct 4, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) stands on the field after the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images “I seen it all on social media and I already got beef with Chiefs fans anyway,” Simmons said while speaking on the DNVR Sports podcast. “That wasn’t a false start. They call that on us… Y’all been cheating y’all whole time y’all had Patrick Mahomes. Refs been cheating for y’all.” He pushed back against the fanbase’s complaints, adding, “My rant is at the Chiefs fans that are delusional enough to think that that was not a false start. It was. Y’all lost at the one-yard line. Ha!” The controversial moment took place after Kansas City held a 24-13 lead late in the third quarter following a 4-yard touchdown pass from Mahomes to tight end Noah Gray. However, Denver scored twice in the fourth quarter to take the lead. Mahomes, who finished the day throwing for 321 yards and three touchdowns, led a frantic seven-play drive to reach the Broncos’ 1-yard line before the game-ending penalty occurred. The narrow defeat handed the Chiefs their second consecutive loss, dropping their record to 5-2 after opening the season with a perfect 5-0 run. After the game, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid admitted he didn’t see a penalty, stating, “I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see [a false start]. One man’s opinion.” Pat echoed his coach’s frustration but took a more resigned approach to the decision. “I have not seen it, but it didn’t catch me,” Mahomes said . “At the end of the day, you have to go with whatever’s called. But a lot of times in those big moments, the little stuff doesn’t get called like that.” However, seeking to bounce back from their sudden slide to 5-2, the Chiefs will return to Arrowhead Stadium this Sunday to face the New York Jets. item.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Finds Home With Reds Or Nats
item.description: Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) is out on a batted ball during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. brings elite speed and power , but his time in New York faces an uncertain future. The Yankees’ second baseman posted a career-high 31 home runs in 2025, yet his consistency remains a major question mark. Fox Sports reports that his 1.7 wins above replacement (bWAR) and 97 OPS+ in 2026 likely cost him a long-term deal. Teams will pay for his talent, but they will not commit to a massive contract without proof of stability. A Fresh Start in Washington The Washington Nationals offer Chisholm a clear path to rebuild his value. Washington finished third in MLB in runs with 821 and slugged at .423 last season, showing they need more punch up the middle. While Nasim Nuñez led the National League with 49 stolen bases, he lacks the power Chisholm provides. The Nationals could use Chisholm to open 2027 as their starting second baseman and help fill the void left by trading Luis García Jr. and Curtis Mead. Chisholm’s move gives him a chance to play either middle infield spot, depending on how the team handles shortstop CJ Abrams. The Reds Need an Offensive Boost With only 75 wins, Cincinnati finished last in the National League Central and urgently needs improvement. MLB hits totaled 1,231 for the Reds, who also recorded the league’s lowest on-base percentage. Chisholm would give them a capable, impact left-handed hitter to balance the lineup. He would likely start at second base, pushing Matt McLain to the bench. McLain has been the primary second baseman for two years but hit a combined .204 during that stretch. Chisholm’s two-time All-Star status would be a massive upgrade for Terry Francona’s order. The market for Chisholm will depend on how teams view his 37.3 stolen bases per season since 2024. He showed he can hit for power, with 80 RBIs in 2025, a year in which he also posted 4.1 wins above replacement. Under Aaron Boone, the Yankees made the postseason eight times over nine years, yet they must determine whether Chisholm belongs in their future. ESPN notes that free agents will come off the board quickly before the league shuts down on Dec. 1.

item.title: NASCAR Confirms Major Qualifying Change for 2027, With More Changes on the Table
item.description: MARTINSVILLE, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 31: Denny Hamlin, driver of the #11 King's Hawaiian Maple Brown Sugar Toyota, climbs into his car during qualifying for the NASCAR Cup Series Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway on October 31, 2026 in Martinsville, Virginia. (Photo by Meg Oliphant/Getty Images) Getty NASCAR is making a significant change to how starting lineups are determined in 2027, and that might not be the only qualifying shakeup coming next season. John Probst, NASCAR’s president of event management, confirmed Friday, Nov. 6, that the sanctioning body will abandon its current qualifying metric when weather or other circumstances prevent a qualifying session from taking place. Beginning in 2027, starting lineups for those races will instead be determined strictly by owner points. The announcement comes during championship weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway, just hours after NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell acknowledged concerns about the existing system during his annual State of the Sport address. And while the new procedure for canceled qualifying sessions is confirmed, NASCAR is also exploring two other possibilities: eliminating the second round of superspeedway qualifying and introducing pit stops into qualifying at select races. NASCAR Is Changing How Starting Lineups Are Set in 2027 For years, NASCAR has relied on a formula to determine starting lineups whenever qualifying cannot be completed. That formula considers several factors, including previous race results and owner points, rather than simply awarding starting positions based on the championship standings. The system has occasionally produced starting grids that look considerably different from the current points order, particularly early in the season when teams have fewer races behind them. That has raised questions about fairness, especially when multiple qualifying sessions are canceled during the opening weeks of a season. Speaking Friday on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio, Probst confirmed that NASCAR will move away from the formula in 2027. #NASCAR ’s John Probst tells @SiriusXMNASCAR that starting lineups for rained out qualifying sessions will be set by Owner’s Points in 2027. Probst also mentions that NASCAR is looking at an All-Star-like qualifying format for some races in 2027 (with a pit stop in the middle).… — Joseph Srigley (@joe_srigley) November 6, 2026 Under the new procedure, owner points alone will determine starting positions when qualifying is canceled. It’s a straightforward adjustment, but one that could have meaningful consequences for teams. A strong position in the owner standings would carry an additional benefit on weekends when drivers never get the opportunity to qualify. The change also removes the influence of individual race results from the canceled-qualifying calculation. Importantly, this applies to races where qualifying cannot be held. James, already assured his PGA Tour card for next year as the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking, had his 14th round of 65 or lower in 13 tournaments since turning pro out of Virginia this summer.
